Slugs for both benchmarks and models were harvested from /sitemap.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml..sitemap-23.xml (24 child sitemaps today, up from 18 on 2026-09-06), not from the /models listing page, which returned only 363 models today versus 486 in the sitemap (confirmed undercount, consistent with prior days). All core pages (index, models, benchmarks, llm-pricing, llm-speed, frontier-ai-models, llm-price-performance) plus /_next/data/<buildId>/benchmarks/<slug>.json for all 426 benchmark slugs and /_next/data/<buildId>/models/<slug>.json for all 486 model slugs (919 endpoints total) were fetched in ONE evaluate_script call using the page's own fetch() behind a 16-way concurrency pool with one retry per URL, saved straight to disk via the filePath option; the only DOM read was __NEXT_DATA__.buildId. Every script began with a location.href guard that threw (not returned) on the wrong page. Zero fetch errors; all 919 endpoints returned usable JSON. normalized.json was then built from raw.json with a separate Python pass (benchmark-data/20260915/benchlm/_normalize.py, kept alongside the outputs) rather than by hand: it reads raw.json's already-fetched values and re-derives ranks/dates mechanically, no score was typed by the agent.
notes: site_stats.modelCount (492) and .benchmarkCount (439) are the site's own self-reported totals and do not equal the sitemap-harvested counts (486 model slugs, 426 benchmark slugs); this same gap existed on 2026-09-06 (417 vs 411, 422 vs 410) and is treated as a known site quirk, not a scraper bug.

raw.json holds the untouched pageProps for every benchmark page, every model page and the index/models/benchmarks/pricing/speed/frontier/price-performance pages, unwrapped from pageProps.pageData one level whenever that nesting is present (checked dynamically per page, not assumed). The homepage leaderboard was normalized to homepageData.leaderboard = {rows, categoryLabels, rankingMode} exactly as on 2026-09-06; it still shipped natively as {rows:[...]} today, not a bare array, so no unwrap was actually needed this run.

The homepage leaderboard still ships as tuple-encoded arrays (39 columns, no column names) inside pageProps.homepageData.leaderboard.rows. Column mapping was re-verified against known models today (Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.6, GLM-5.3-Flash, Muse Spark 1.3) and is unchanged from 20260906: [1]=model, [2]=slug, [3]=provider, [8]=contextWindow, [10]=inputPrice, [11]=outputPrice, [12]=blendedPrice, [13]=tokensPerSecond, [14]=latency seconds, [15]=Elo, [17]=release date (ISO), [26]=displayScore, [27]=full-precision overall score, [30]=category scores array in categoryLabels order Agentic, Coding, Reasoning, Multimodal & Grounded, Knowledge, Multilingual, Instruction Following, Math.

rank for per-benchmark records is the position in the leaderboard order the site publishes for that benchmark (no numeric rank field in the payload). Zero benchmarks had a null-score entry today (checked all 426), so no rank gaps arise in practice.

rank for Overall was computed by sorting the 232 rows with a non-null displayScore (row[26], the ranking-eligible set) by full-precision overall score (row[27]) descending; the score reported is the rounded displayScore (row[26]). This matches the 20260906 convention exactly (that day's write-up says 'sorting the 232 scored models (row[26] non-null) by full-precision overall score (row[27])'); an earlier draft of today's normalizer filtered on row[27] instead of row[26] and was caught and corrected before normalized.json was written, since row[27] is populated for all 486 models (including non-ranking-eligible ones like Muse Spark 1.3) while row[26] is populated for only 232. Category and Elo ranks are likewise computed by sorting the rows with a non-null value at that column descending, not gated by ranking eligibility.

Per-benchmark records take cost_usd from the model detail page's pricing.blendedPrice, context_window from pricing.contextWindow falling back to the benchmark row's own contextWindow, and date from the model detail page's model.releaseLabel. 1511 of 9572 benchmark-leaderboard entries (about 16%) reference a model slug absent from modelsDetail (models the benchmark page still lists but that have dropped out of the sitemap/model catalogue); for those, cost_usd and date are omitted and context_window falls back to the benchmark row's own value. Overall / Category / Elo records take cost_usd, context_window and date from the homepage row columns [12], [8] and [17]. Fields are omitted (not fabricated as null or 0) when no source has a value.

Payload shape drift found today: 3 of 426 benchmark detail pages (gaia, ifbench, scicode) ship their metric label under a top-level 'metric' key instead of 'format', with a 'source'/'paper' field pair instead of 'paperUrl'/'authors'. The normalizer falls back to benchmark.metric when benchmark.format is absent, so this did not lose any rows; flagging it here because it is exactly the kind of unlabeled shape drift the site is known for.

Benchmark name collisions exist across slugs; source_url disambiguates (benchmark pages use https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/<pageSlug>; Overall records use https://benchlm.ai/models/<slug>; Category records use https://benchlm.ai/<categoryKey>; Elo records use https://benchlm.ai/).
No values were estimated or invented. Missing data is omitted. Zero fetch errors; all 426 benchmark and 486 model endpoints returned HTTP 200.

Browser contention today was worse than a typical run: the first isolated page opened for this scrape (benchlm-rescrape-20260915) was navigated away to https://www.designarena.ai/leaderboard mid-run by another concurrent agent's blind navigate_page call (that tool has no pageId parameter and always acts on whichever page is globally selected at the instant it fires, which is a race even when select_page immediately precedes it in the same turn). That page was closed rather than recovered, and a fresh isolated page (benchlm-rescrape-20260915b) was opened in its place. In the course of fixing this, one accidental navigate_page from this agent briefly sent the artificial-analysis and terminal-bench agents' own tabs to benchlm.ai; both self-healed via their own href guards within a few retries. No data was written from any of the wrong-page states; every guard threw before any fetch or save happened on a mismatched host.

This site mirrors other publishers' benchmarks rather than running its own evaluations. Treat its rows as corroboration and prefer the original source (Artificial Analysis, Vals, LiveBench, Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, etc.) where they disagree. No specific disagreement with an original source was checked in this run beyond the six named models below.
